Target:   axios/axios @ 9f0f4dd · checked 2026-11-22
Decision: 🔴 Do not adopt — Do not use: malicious release
Confidence: high — Malware advisories from two sources agree, and the latest version was checked with all vulnerability sources answering.

No, do not install axios 1.14.1: it is flagged as malware and was removed from npm. Use the latest
release, 1.21.1, which has no known issues, an MIT licence and an actively maintained project.

Follow-up
 • Was 1.14.1 ever installed or deployed anywhere in your systems?

Why
 🔴 Security: Malicious release: 1.14.1 (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9, MAL-2026-2307). (CRA Art. 13(5))
   • Version 1.14.1 is a known malicious release (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9, MAL-2026-2307): do not
     install it.
     "Malicious code in axios (npm)" → https://osv.dev/vulnerability/MAL-2026-2307 ✔
   • Version 1.14.1 of axios is flagged as malware (critical). Do not install it.
     "Malware in axios" → https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9 ✔
   • Version 1.14.1 is no longer on npm. Removal like this often happens to malicious releases.
     "version 1.14.1 is no longer on npm (removed; this often happens to malicious releases); repo taken from…" → https://github.com/axios/axios ✔
 🟢 Licence: MIT licence: permissive, keep the copyright notice.
   • axios uses the MIT licence. You can use it commercially if you keep the copyright and licence
     notice.
     "Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy of this software" → https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/9f0f4ddfe72b4c06afafe1a658e6ee53d35b5760/LICENSE#L3 ✔
 🟢 Maintenance: Active repository, not archived, recent commits and releases.
   • The axios project is actively maintained: it is not archived, the last commit was on
     2026-11-18, and the latest release was on 2026-11-09.
     ""head_commit_date": "2026-11-18T05:08:24Z"" → https://github.com/axios/axios ✔

What to do next
 1. Do not install 1.14.1 (or 0.30.4, also flagged). Pin axios to 1.21.1 or newer instead.
     Source: "Malware in axios"
     → https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9
 2. Search lockfiles, build caches and deployed images for 1.14.1. If it was ever installed, treat
   that machine as compromised: rotate its secrets and review it.
     Source: "version 1.14.1 is no longer on npm (removed; this often happens to malicious
       releases);…"
     → https://github.com/axios/axios
 3. Pin to 1.21.1 and re-check for advisories before each upgrade.
     Source: ""malware": [], "vulnerabilities": []"
     → https://github.com/axios/axios
